title: Research 3/9: overruling doctrines - conditions and reasoning burden for departing from precedent
description: Research agenda item 3 (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:51). Survey how apex courts justify departing from their own precedent: the UK Practice Statement of 1966 (a court granting itself overruling power) and subsequent House of Lords / UK Supreme Court practice, the US stare decisis factors actually recited in landmark reversals (quality of reasoning, workability, reliance interests, changed facts and changed understanding), prospective overruling, and the civil-law analogues where relevant. Derive: what conditions and reasoning burden should agent overruling require, per authority tier. Output docs/precedent-research/03-overruling-doctrines.md. Web research, tagged claims, mandatory implications section.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE (create only this; touch no other file): docs/precedent-research/03-overruling-doctrines.md. Create the parent directory with mkdir -p (idempotent and race-safe: the nine research tasks run in parallel, share no file, and no bootstrap root serializes them). Do NOT create or edit docs/precedent-research/README.md - that index is owned solely by the epic join T-348 (F1 single-owner rule).

WEB RESEARCH IS REQUIRED (coordinator decision D7): at least 5 named sources, of which at least 3 are primary (a judgment with its case name and citation, a statute or code article, an official practice statement or court rule, or a named-author treatise / peer-reviewed article). Every source is listed in a final Sources section with a retrievable identifier (case name plus citation, or URL plus retrieval date). Parametric-only claims with no locatable source are tagged SPECULATION, never ESTABLISHED.

EVERY substantive claim carries exactly one tag: ESTABLISHED (attributable to a named source in the Sources section), ANALOGY (a mapping from legal doctrine onto agent mechanics - the mapping is this agent's inference, not the source's claim), or SPECULATION (neither). An untagged substantive claim is a defect and grounds for REJECT. Basis: roadmap Part V principle 5, no fabricated rigor (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:96).

For each finding state which schema field, CLI subcommand, or protocol rule it demands, or state explicitly that it demands none.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Extends, does not duplicate': for every doctrine that already has a partial implementation in this repo, cite it by file:line and say whether the finding EXTENDS the existing record or would DUPLICATE it. The candidates the scout already located: note taxonomy DECISION/DEVIATION/TRADEOFF/OPEN-QUESTION (ORCHESTRATION.md:69-77), the reopen verb with its mandatory-reasoning gate (.harness/bin/blackboard.py:470-517, ORCHESTRATION.md:58-67), the P-number ledger (state.json evolution.accepted_mutations), prose P-number citations in ORCHESTRATION.md, recontext.py append-only cited-evidence log, events.jsonl semantic event floor. Rationale: the corpus records a measured non-additive interaction where stacking one more layer that re-does existing verification REGRESSED performance (papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:8, Table 3 RQ3a, '+ system_prompt only' -2.3pp; p.9 'Components interact non-additively').

MANDATORY: state at least one finding that CUTS AGAINST the roadmap brief or the coordinator decision memo where the sources support one. If the sources support none, say so explicitly and say why - a document with zero friction against its own commissioning brief is treated as unverified cheerleading.
NO CODE and NO edits under .harness/ or to PRECEDENT.md. Research tasks have no build dependencies and must create none.

Verification tier: DOC TIER per P-024 (proportional verification) - the verifier does a BRIEF replay (file exists at the exact path; every substantive claim tagged; Sources section present with the required counts; the two mandatory sections present; spot-check that 2 named sources exist), NOT a full adversarial replay. Hand off with blackboard.py handoff --to-role verifier (never self-mark done). The handoff note must name the 3 findings that most change the schema, each with the tag it carries.

MUST derive a concrete, checkable overruling burden PER D4 TIER: who may overturn a tier-1 operator decision, a tier-2 constitutional decision, a tier-3 verdicted decision, and a tier-4 persuasive note - and what the record must contain in each case (citation of the overruled record, the factor(s) relied on, the new authority's tier).

MUST decide and justify whether agent overruling REUSES the existing reopen mechanism (blackboard.py reopen: terminal-state-only, mandatory --note, logs task_reopened to events.jsonl - .harness/bin/blackboard.py:470-517, ORCHESTRATION.md:58-67) or requires a NEW verb, and say what the reopen verb structurally lacks for precedent-level overruling (it is scoped to tasks, not decisions).

MUST state whether silent divergence is detectable at all in this substrate, and if so from what evidence - the brief calls silent divergence a violation (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:37), so name the signal or say plainly that v0 cannot detect it.

MUST address the reliance-interest analogue: what does it cost when a precedent that later work already built on is overruled, and does the record need a 'relied on by' back-reference to make that cost visible?
